data.comment: Alarms status line after saving an alarm.

data.comment: Window that comes with a repeating alarm sound, under what the alarm found.

data.name: PickSoundTitle

data.name: PickSoundFileType

data.name: DialogDefaultTitle
data.comment: Title of an alarm's pop-up dialog when the alarm gives none.

data.name: CheckTimer
data.comment: Alarm editor, Check pick list: the check that fires at a date and time. (The AI agent is given its own English names for the checks; this is only what the screen shows.)

data.name: CheckTimerNote
data.value: Fires at a specific date and time, and optionally repeats on a fixed interval thereafter. Use for reminders and anything scheduled. An occurrence that came due while the app was closed fires at the next start rather than being skipped.
data.comment: Alarm editor, under the Check pick list when Date / time is picked: what the check does.

data.name: CheckIntel
data.comment: Alarm editor, Check pick list: the check that fires on a sighting reported in an intel channel.

data.name: CheckIntelNote
data.value: Fires when someone reports a pilot near what you are watching: your characters while they are undocked, your characters wherever they are, or a list of systems, each with a range in jumps. Reads the intel channels already being parsed under Settings → Chat Logs.
data.comment: Alarm editor, under the Check pick list when Intel report is picked. "Settings → Chat Logs" names the place in the Settings window.

data.name: CheckIntelKillsNote
data.value: Kills there with hostile pilots among the attackers count too: a kill places its attackers in that system.
data.comment: Alarm editor, under the Check pick list when Intel report is picked; follows CheckIntelNote as its next sentence. A kill (a killmail) whose attackers include hostile pilots counts as a sighting of them. Hostile = not yours and not at positive standing.

data.name: CheckShipUndock
data.comment: Alarm editor, Check pick list: the check that fires when one of your characters undocks.

data.name: CheckShipUndockNote
data.value: Fires when one of your characters undocks. Optionally only from named stations, structures, systems or regions, only in named hulls or ship classes, and only in a given state — fit or not fit, jump fuel lower than a number or not, ammunition lower than a number or not. Every filter narrows, so two alarms can be set to cover different undocks rather than the same one twice. The undock is seen by the location poll within about ten seconds; what was aboard is judged from the last asset snapshot, which ESI refreshes hourly, and each match says how old that was.
data.comment: Alarm editor, under the Check pick list when Ship undocks is picked.

data.name: CheckUndockedTooLong
data.comment: Alarm editor, Check pick list: the check that wakes you when a ship sits in space too long after an undock or a jump.

data.name: CheckUndockedTooLongNote
data.value: Wakes you up. Fires in up to three stages when one of your characters in a named hull or ship class undocks and is still sitting in that same system after a number of seconds — a freighter or jump freighter on a tether while its pilot dozes off. Or, ticked for jump arrivals, when a jump-capable hull has landed by jump drive or bridge and is still in space — the thirty seconds after a jump. Docking, leaving the system or logging off ends it. Pressing the dialog's button, or replying anything at all to the agent, quiets it for a while; when that lapses and the ship is still there, the stages start over. Each stage has its own actions — TTS direct or the agent to say the stage's line, a dialog, a sound that repeats until acknowledged. Repeat and cooldown do not apply.
data.comment: Alarm editor, under the Check pick list when Undocked too long is picked. "TTS direct" is the action that speaks without the agent.

data.name: CheckStoreOrder
data.comment: Alarm editor, Check pick list: the check that fires on what happens to EVE Mail store orders.

data.name: CheckStoreOrderNote
data.value: Fires on what happens to EVE Mail store orders: a new order placed — with the store, the buyer, the item, the price, and whether it is in stock or has to be built — an order newly fillable from stock or newly in build, a contract issued for it, the contract accepted (the order complete), or the order canceled. Tick the kinds you want. Orders added by hand in the Order Tracker are not reported. Runs the moment the store books or updates an order.
data.comment: Alarm editor, under the Check pick list when Store order events is picked. Order Tracker is the name of a tool in the app.

data.name: CheckMarketContract
data.comment: Alarm editor, Check pick list: the check that fires when an item is offered at or below a price.

data.name: CheckMarketContractNote
data.value: Fires when an item is listed at or below a price you name — on the market, in public contracts, or both. Reads the markets configured under Settings → Market and the public contracts already being swept, so it sees what those cover and nothing else.
data.comment: Alarm editor, under the Check pick list when Market / contract price is picked. "Settings → Market" names the place in the Settings window.

data.name: CheckSql
data.comment: Alarm editor, Check pick list: the check that runs a database query of your own.

data.name: CheckSqlNote
data.value: Runs a SELECT against the local EVE Console database on an interval and fires on the rows it returns, or on there being none. Use when no purpose-built check fits. Only SELECT is permitted.
data.comment: Alarm editor, under the Check pick list when Database query is picked. SELECT is an SQL word; keep it.

data.name: TimerAtLabel
data.comment: Alarm editor, Date / time check: label over the date and time the alarm fires at.

data.name: TimerAtNote
data.value: When to fire, ISO 8601. Include an offset (e.g. 2026-08-04T18:00:00-05:00) or a trailing Z for UTC; a bare local time is read as the machine's local time.
data.comment: Alarm editor, Date / time check, under the date and time. ISO 8601 names the date format; keep it and the example as they are.

data.name: TimerRepeatLabel
data.comment: Alarm editor, Date / time check: label of the box for how often, in seconds, the alarm repeats.

data.name: TimerRepeatNote
data.value: Optional. Repeat this often after the first firing. Omit or 0 for a one-time timer.
data.comment: Alarm editor, Date / time check, under the repeat box.

data.name: IntelSystemsLabel
data.comment: Alarm editor, Intel report check: label of the solar systems to watch.

data.name: IntelSystemsNote
data.value: Systems to watch, e.g. {0} or {1}. Add each one; with Jumps at 0, only these systems are watched.
data.comment: Alarm editor, Intel report check, under Systems (shown when Watch around is Systems). {0} and {1} are two systems' names, filled in as the game names them in the interface language (Jita, Amarr). "Jumps" is the setting below it (IntelJumpsLabel).

data.name: IntelJumpsLabel
data.comment: Alarm editor, Intel report check: label of the number of gate jumps to watch around each character or system.

data.name: IntelJumpsNote
data.value: How many gate jumps out from each character or system to watch. 0 means their own system only. Capped at 15 — past that it stops being a neighbourhood.
data.comment: Alarm editor, Intel report check, under Jumps.

data.name: IntelMinPlayersLabel
data.comment: Alarm editor, Intel report check: label of the least number of pilots a report must name.

data.name: IntelMinPlayersNote
data.value: Only fire when the report is of at least this many pilots. Default 1.
data.comment: Alarm editor, Intel report check, under Min players.

data.name: IntelIgnoreNvLabel
data.comment: Alarm editor, Intel report check: tick box to skip reports marked "no visual".

data.name: IntelIgnoreNvNote
data.value: Skip reports flagged NV (no visual) — someone relaying a contact they cannot actually see.
data.comment: Alarm editor, Intel report check, beside Ignore no visual. NV is the tag intel channels use; keep it.

data.name: UndockFromLabel
data.comment: Alarm editor, Ship undocks check: label of the list of places to watch undocks from.

data.name: UndockFromNote
data.value: Optional. Station, structure, solar system or region names, any mix. Matches an undock from any of them; leave empty for anywhere.
data.comment: Alarm editor, Ship undocks check, under Undocking from.

data.name: FlyingLabel
data.comment: Alarm editor, Ship undocks and Undocked too long checks: label of the list of hulls and ship classes to watch.

data.name: UndockShipsNote
data.value: Optional. Hull names ("{0}"), ship classes ("{1}", "{2}") or "Pod", any mix. Matches any of them; leave empty for any ship.
data.comment: Alarm editor, Ship undocks check, under Flying. {0} is a hull's name and {1}, {2} ship classes' names, filled in as the game names them in the interface language (Rifter, Cruiser, Titan). "Pod" is what is typed in the list to mean a capsule, so keep it as Pod.

data.name: UndockFitLabel
data.comment: Alarm editor, Ship undocks check: label of the choice Any / Not fit / Fit — whether the ship has anything fitted.

data.name: UndockFitNote
data.value: "Not fit": nothing at all in any slot. "Fit": something is. A pod or shuttle has no slots and matches neither. Judged from the last asset snapshot, which ESI refreshes only hourly — it can be up to an hour behind what is aboard right now.
data.comment: Alarm editor, Ship undocks check, under Fit. "Not fit" and "Fit" are the choices; use the same words as OptionNotFit and OptionFit.

data.name: UndockFuelLabel
data.comment: Alarm editor, Ship undocks check: label of the choice about the jump fuel aboard.

data.name: UndockFuelNote
data.value: Jump-capable hulls only; any other hull matches neither. The units are of the isotope the hull's jump drive burns, fuel bay and cargo hold together — as of the last asset snapshot, which ESI refreshes only hourly, so fuel loaded in the last hour may not be counted yet.
data.comment: Alarm editor, Ship undocks check, under Jump fuel.

data.name: UndockAmmoLabel
data.comment: Alarm editor, Ship undocks check: label of the choice about the ammunition aboard.

data.name: UndockAmmoNote
data.value: Per fitted turret or launcher: the rounds it can load that are aboard, loaded plus cargo, all compatible types together. "Lower than": any weapon short. "Not lower than": weapons fitted and none short. An energy turret only needs one crystal. A ship without weapons matches neither. As of the last asset snapshot, which ESI refreshes only hourly — ammunition loaded in the last hour may not be counted yet.
data.comment: Alarm editor, Ship undocks check, under Ammunition. "Lower than" and "Not lower than" are the choices; use the same words as OptionLowerThan and OptionNotLowerThan.

data.name: SuffixUnits
data.comment: Alarm editor, Ship undocks check: the word after a number of jump fuel or ammunition units, as in "Lower than [5,000] units".

data.name: OptionAny
data.comment: Alarm editor, Ship undocks check, choices under Fit, Jump fuel and Ammunition: the one that does not filter.

data.name: OptionNotFit
data.comment: Alarm editor, Ship undocks check, choice under Fit: nothing at all is fitted.

data.name: OptionFit
data.comment: Alarm editor, Ship undocks check, choice under Fit: something is fitted.

data.name: OptionLowerThan
data.comment: Alarm editor, Ship undocks check, choice under Jump fuel and Ammunition, before a number: less than that is aboard.

data.name: OptionNotLowerThan
data.comment: Alarm editor, Ship undocks check, choice under Jump fuel and Ammunition, before a number: at least that is aboard.

data.name: AdriftArrivalsLabel
data.comment: Alarm editor, Undocked too long check: tick box that starts the clock when a ship lands by jump drive or bridge instead of when it undocks.

data.name: AdriftArrivalsNote
data.value: Ticked: the clock starts when a jump-capable hull lands in a system no stargate leads to from where it was — a jump drive or a bridge — and is still in space; only hulls with a jump drive are watched, and an empty Flying list means all of them. Unticked: the clock starts at an undock, any hull, and Flying must name what to watch.
data.comment: Alarm editor, Undocked too long check, beside Jump arrivals. Flying is the list of hulls below it (FlyingLabel).

data.name: AdriftShipsNote
data.value: Hull names ("{0}") or ship classes ("{1}", "{2}", "{3}"), any mix. Only these are watched — or, for jump arrivals, leave it empty for every jump-capable hull.
data.comment: Alarm editor, Undocked too long check, under Flying. {0} is a hull's name and {1} to {3} ship classes' names, filled in as the game names them in the interface language (Rhea, Freighter, Jump Freighter, Hauler).

data.name: AdriftStageLabel
data.comment: Alarm editor, Undocked too long check: a stage's own setting, before a number of seconds. {0} is the stage's number.

data.name: AdriftStage1Note
data.value: The first, gentler stage. Untick to skip it.
data.comment: Alarm editor, Undocked too long check, under stage 1's number of seconds.

data.name: AdriftStage2Note
data.comment: Alarm editor, Undocked too long check, under stage 2's number of seconds.

data.name: AdriftStage3Note
data.value: The last resort — pair it with a Sound action set to repeat until acknowledged. Untick to skip it.
data.comment: Alarm editor, Undocked too long check, under stage 3's number of seconds. Sound is the name of an action.

data.name: SuffixSecondsUndocked
data.comment: Alarm editor, Undocked too long check: after a stage's number, as in "STAGE 1 after [180] seconds undocked".

data.name: AdriftSnoozeLabel
data.comment: Alarm editor, Undocked too long check: label of how many minutes an acknowledgement keeps the alarm quiet.

data.name: AdriftSnoozeNote
data.value: How long a reply or the dialog's button keeps this quiet while the ship stays undocked — long enough to wait on a titan bridge. Then the stages start over.
data.comment: Alarm editor, Undocked too long check, under Quiet after an acknowledgement.

data.name: SuffixMinutes
data.comment: Alarm editor: the word after a number of minutes, as in "[30] minutes".

data.name: StoreNewOrdersLabel
data.comment: Alarm editor, Store order events check: tick box for one kind of event.

data.name: StoreNewOrdersNote
data.value: With the store, the buyer, the item, the price, and its state on arrival.
data.comment: Alarm editor, Store order events check, beside New order placed: what the alarm says about a new order.

data.name: StoreInStockLabel
data.comment: Alarm editor, Store order events check: tick box for one kind of event.

data.name: StoreInStockNote
data.value: An order the fulfilment pass now finds on the shelf — contract it.
data.comment: Alarm editor, Store order events check, beside Newly fillable from stock.

data.name: StoreInBuildLabel
data.comment: Alarm editor, Store order events check: tick box for one kind of event.

data.name: StoreInBuildNote
data.value: An industry job now claimed for the order.
data.comment: Alarm editor, Store order events check, beside Newly in build.

data.name: StoreContractedLabel
data.comment: Alarm editor, Store order events check: tick box for one kind of event.

data.name: StoreContractedNote
data.value: A contract to the buyer carrying the order, awaiting acceptance.
data.comment: Alarm editor, Store order events check, beside Contract issued.

data.name: StoreAcceptedLabel
data.comment: Alarm editor, Store order events check: tick box for one kind of event.

data.name: StoreCanceledLabel
data.comment: Alarm editor, Store order events check: tick box for one kind of event.

data.name: StoreCanceledNote
data.value: By the buyer's mail, a rejected contract, or by hand.
data.comment: Alarm editor, Store order events check, beside Order canceled: the ways an order is canceled.

data.name: StoreStoreLabel
data.comment: Alarm editor, Store order events check: label of the one store to watch.

data.name: StoreStoreNote
data.value: Optional: only this store, by name. Blank for every store.
data.comment: Alarm editor, Store order events check, under Store.

data.name: MarketItemLabel
data.comment: Alarm editor, Market / contract price check: label of the item to watch.

data.name: MarketItemNote
data.value: Exact item name, e.g. "{0}" or "{1}". Must match the type name exactly; a name that does not resolve matches nothing.
data.comment: Alarm editor, Market / contract price check, under Item. {0} and {1} are two items' names, filled in as the game names them in the interface language (Sigil, Imperial Navy Slicer).

data.name: MarketMaxPriceLabel
data.comment: Alarm editor, Market / contract price check: label of the highest price per unit, in ISK.

data.name: MarketMaxPriceNote
data.value: Fire when the price per unit is at or below this, in ISK.
data.comment: Alarm editor, Market / contract price check, under Max unit price.

data.name: MarketMinQtyLabel
data.comment: Alarm editor, Market / contract price check: label of the least number on offer.

data.name: MarketMinQtyNote
data.value: Only fire when at least this many are on offer in the one listing. Default 1.
data.comment: Alarm editor, Market / contract price check, under Min quantity.

data.name: MarketSourceLabel
data.comment: Alarm editor, Market / contract price check: label of where to look — the market, contracts or both.

data.name: MarketSourceNote
data.comment: Alarm editor, Market / contract price check, under Source. "both" is the choice OptionBoth; use the same word.

data.name: MarketMarketLabel
data.comment: Alarm editor, Market / contract price check: label of the one configured market to watch.

data.name: MarketMarketNote
data.value: Optional. Restrict the market side to one configured market by name, e.g. "Jita". Omit to watch them all.
data.comment: Alarm editor, Market / contract price check, under Market. Jita is a place in the game; keep it.

data.name: MarketBundledLabel
data.comment: Alarm editor, Market / contract price check: tick box to include contracts holding other items too.

data.name: MarketBundledNote
data.value: Include contracts holding more than just this item. Off by default, because the asking price then covers the other contents too and the resulting price per unit is not a real one.
data.comment: Alarm editor, Market / contract price check, beside Bundled contracts.

data.name: OptionBoth
data.comment: Alarm editor, Market / contract price check, Source choices: the market and public contracts.

data.name: OptionMarket
data.comment: Alarm editor, Market / contract price check, Source choices: the market only.

data.name: OptionContracts
data.comment: Alarm editor, Market / contract price check, Source choices: public contracts only.

data.name: SqlQueryLabel
data.comment: Alarm editor, Database query check: label of the box for the SQL query.

data.name: SqlQueryNote
data.value: The SELECT to run. Only SELECT (or a WITH…SELECT) is allowed. Keep it small and add a LIMIT — it runs on every check. Include a stable identifying column and name it in key_column.
data.comment: Alarm editor, Database query check, under the query. SELECT, WITH and LIMIT are SQL words, and key_column is the setting below it (Key column); keep them.

data.name: SqlKeyColumnLabel
data.comment: Alarm editor, Database query check: label of the column that identifies each row.

data.name: SqlKeyColumnNote
data.value: Column holding a stable, unique identifier for each row — an Id or similar. This is what stops a row being announced twice. Never nominate something that changes between runs, or the alarm will fire on every check. Defaults to a column called Id if the query has one, otherwise the whole row is used as its own key.
data.comment: Alarm editor, Database query check, under Key column. Id is a column name; keep it.

data.name: SqlLabelColumnLabel
data.comment: Alarm editor, Database query check: label of the column whose value is the alert's text.

data.name: SqlLabelColumnNote
data.value: Optional column to use as the alert text. Defaults to the whole row.
data.comment: Alarm editor, Database query check, under Label column.

data.name: SqlModeLabel
data.comment: Alarm editor, Database query check: label of the choice between firing on rows and firing on none.

data.name: SqlModeNote
data.value: 'present' (default) fires on rows returned. 'absent' fires when the query returns nothing at all, and re-arms once rows come back — for watching that something expected has stopped happening.
data.comment: Alarm editor, Database query check, under Mode. 'present' and 'absent' are the choices; use the same words as OptionPresent and OptionAbsent.

data.name: OptionPresent
data.comment: Alarm editor, Database query check, Mode choices: fire on the rows the query returns.

data.name: OptionAbsent
data.comment: Alarm editor, Database query check, Mode choices: fire when the query returns no rows.

data.name: MatchesAndMore
data.comment: Last line of the list of matches under an alarm's alert or dialog, after a bullet. {0} is how many more matches there are.

data.name: IntelHostileReported
data.comment: Title of an Intel report alarm's alert or dialog for one report; the systems follow after a dash.

data.name: IntelHostileReportsOne
data.comment: Title of an Intel report alarm's alert or dialog for several reports; the systems follow after a dash. {0} is the number of reports. (Exactly one reads IntelHostileReported instead.)

data.name: IntelHostileReportsOther
data.comment: Title of an Intel report alarm's alert or dialog for several reports; the systems follow after a dash. {0} is the number of reports.

data.name: IntelSaidReportedOne
data.comment: Spoken when an Intel report alarm fires. {0} is the number of hostiles, {1} the system.

data.name: IntelSaidReportedOther
data.comment: Spoken when an Intel report alarm fires. {0} is the number of hostiles, {1} the system.

data.name: IntelSaidReportedAtOne
data.comment: Spoken when an Intel report alarm fires. {0} is the number of hostiles, {1} the system, {2} how far away it is (IntelSaidHere or IntelSaidJumpsOut).

data.name: IntelSaidReportedAtOther
data.comment: Spoken when an Intel report alarm fires. {0} is the number of hostiles, {1} the system, {2} how far away it is (IntelSaidHere or IntelSaidJumpsOut).

data.name: IntelSaidHere
data.comment: Spoken, in IntelSaidReportedAt: the hostiles are in the watched system itself.

data.name: IntelSaidJumpsOutOne
data.comment: Spoken, in IntelSaidReportedAt: how many gate jumps from the watched system. {0} is the number of jumps.

data.name: IntelSaidJumpsOutOther
data.comment: Spoken, in IntelSaidReportedAt: how many gate jumps from the watched system. {0} is the number of jumps.

data.name: IntelSaidFlying
data.comment: Spoken when an Intel report alarm fires: the hostiles' ships. {0} is one hull with its article (HullA, HullAn) or a list of hull names (ListAnd, ListAndMore).

data.name: IntelSaidPilotsAndMore
data.comment: Spoken when an Intel report alarm fires: the pilots reported. {0} is five names, joined by commas; {1} how many more there are.

data.name: SaidSentence
data.comment: Spoken: a sentence that is only names, or a note copied from an intel report. {0} is that text; only the full stop is translated.

data.name: IntelSaidOnKill
data.comment: Spoken by an intel alarm after the hostiles' count, hulls and names, when they were seen as attackers on a kill rather than reported in a channel. Goes into SaidSentence ("{0}."), so no full stop here.

data.name: UnknownSystem
data.comment: Spoken in place of a solar system's name when it is not known, as in "3 hostiles reported in an unknown system."

data.name: HullA
data.comment: Spoken or in an alert's title: a ship by its hull name, when the name starts with a consonant — "a Rifter". {0} is the hull name, from the game. In a language without articles, just {0}.

data.name: HullAn
data.comment: Spoken or in an alert's title: a ship by its hull name, when the name starts with a vowel — "an Abaddon". {0} is the hull name, from the game. In a language without articles, just {0}.

data.name: HullPod
data.comment: Spoken or in an alert's title, in place of a hull: the character is in a capsule (pod).

data.name: HullShip
data.comment: Spoken or in an alert's title, in place of a hull whose name is not known.

data.name: ListAnd
data.comment: Spoken: the end of a list of hull names. {0} is the names before the last, joined by commas; {1} the last.

data.name: ListAndMore
data.comment: Spoken: a list of hull names cut short. {0} is the first three, joined by commas.

data.name: SaidAndMore
data.comment: Spoken at the end of an alarm's announcement when more happened than was read out. {0} is how many more.

data.name: UndockTitle
data.comment: Title of a Ship undocks alarm's alert or dialog. {0} is the character, {1} the ship with its article (HullA, HullAn, HullPod, HullShip).

data.name: UndocksOne
data.comment: Title of a Ship undocks alarm's alert or dialog for several undocks. {0} is the number of undocks.

data.name: UndocksOther
data.comment: Title of a Ship undocks alarm's alert or dialog for several undocks. {0} is the number of undocks.

data.name: UndockSaid
data.comment: Spoken when a Ship undocks alarm fires. {0} is the character, {1} the solar system, {2} the ship with its article (HullA, HullAn, HullPod, HullShip).

data.name: UndockSaidProblems
data.comment: Spoken when a Ship undocks alarm fires and something is missing. {0} is the character, {1} the solar system, {2} the ship with its article (HullA, HullAn, HullPod, HullShip), {3} what is missing (UndockNothingFitted, UndockLowFuel and the rest), joined by commas.

data.name: UndockNothingFitted
data.comment: Spoken, in UndockSaidProblems: the ship left with nothing fitted.

data.name: UndockNoFuel
data.comment: Spoken, in UndockSaidProblems: the ship left with no jump fuel.

data.name: UndockLowFuel
data.comment: Spoken, in UndockSaidProblems: the ship left short of jump fuel.

data.name: UndockNoAmmo
data.comment: Spoken, in UndockSaidProblems: the ship left with no ammunition.

data.name: UndockLowAmmo
data.comment: Spoken, in UndockSaidProblems: the ship left short of ammunition.

data.name: AdriftTitle
data.comment: Title of an Undocked too long (wake-up call) alarm's alert or dialog. {0} is the person's name as the agent knows it, or AdriftCapsuleer.

data.name: AdriftBodyLanded
data.value: {0}'s {1} landed in {2} {3} ago and has not docked. Press I'm awake to keep this quiet for {4} minutes while the ship stays out.
data.comment: Body of a wake-up call's alert or dialog, after a jump arrival. {0} is the character, {1} the hull name or AdriftPod, {2} the solar system, {3} how long ago (SpanSeconds, SpanMinutes), {4} a number of minutes. "I'm awake" is the dialog's button (ButtonImAwake); use the same words.

data.name: AdriftBodyUndocked
data.value: {0}'s {1} has been undocked in {2} for {3} and has not docked. Press I'm awake to keep this quiet for {4} minutes while the ship stays out.
data.comment: Body of a wake-up call's alert or dialog, after an undock. {0} is the character, {1} the hull name or AdriftPod, {2} the solar system, {3} how long (SpanSeconds, SpanMinutes), {4} a number of minutes. "I'm awake" is the dialog's button (ButtonImAwake); use the same words.

data.name: AdriftLandedStage1
